title: SBTA032 Examination Practice - Introduction and Innate Immunity

questions.question: SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Innate immunity is an antigen-specific immune response.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Innate immunity relies on components that are already formed before infection.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Innate immunity develops a stronger memory response after repeated exposure to the same pathogen.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Tissue macrophages can recruit neutrophils to an infected site.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Disease is defined as the ability of a pathogen to enter a host and multiply.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Naturally acquired passive immunity usually provides immediate but short-term protection.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Adaptive immunity is the first line of host defence and has no memory.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - PAMPs are conserved microbial components detected by pattern-recognition molecules.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - DAMPs may be released from necrotic cells and contribute to tissue damage.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Recognition of a pathogen by PRRs can promote cytokine and chemokine production.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Squamous epithelium of the skin acts as a physical barrier.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Peristalsis is a chemical defence mechanism of mucous membranes.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Hydrochloric acid contributes to innate defence by producing a low pH in the stomach.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Normal flora can protect the host by competing with pathogens for nutrients and colonisation sites.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - The complement system can be activated only through the classical pathway.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Lactoferrin and transferrin restrict bacterial growth by competing for iron.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - The principal function of neutrophils is antigen presentation to T lymphocytes.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Natural killer cells can kill virus-infected cells and altered self cells.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Eosinophils are important in defence against certain parasites.
SECTION A: TRUE OR FALSE (1 mark) - Blood monocytes are precursors of tissue macrophages.
SECTION B: SINGLE BEST ANSWER (2 marks) - Which statement best defines immunology?
options: The study of immune-system components and functions in defence against infection
The study of microbial metabolism only
The study of inherited blood groups only
The study of drug absorption and excretion
questions.answer: The study of immune-system components and functions in defence against infection

questions.question: SECTION B: SINGLE BEST ANSWER (2 marks) - Which antibody pattern is expected during a secondary response to a previously encountered antigen?
options: A rapid rise in IgG with little or no rise in IgM
A rapid rise in IgM with no IgG production
An equal immediate rise in all five immunoglobulin classes
No antibody production because innate immunity prevents it
questions.answer: A rapid rise in IgG with little or no rise in IgM

questions.question: SECTION B: SINGLE BEST ANSWER (2 marks) - Loss of self-tolerance most directly results in which immune-system disorder?
SECTION B: SINGLE BEST ANSWER (2 marks) - Immunoglobulin classes are distinguished mainly by structural differences in which region?

Disulfide bonds between light chains only

SECTION D: STRUCTURED QUESTION (10 marks) - Distinguish naturally acquired active immunity from naturally acquired passive immunity. Include the route of acquisition, whether the recipient produces an immune response, the speed of protection and the expected duration. Relate your answer to the primary and secondary antibody responses.

SECTION D: STRUCTURED QUESTION (10 marks) - Describe the mechanical, chemical and biological barriers of innate immunity. Give relevant examples from the skin, gastrointestinal tract, respiratory tract, tears or saliva, and normal flora, and explain how each limits infection.

SECTION D: APPLIED QUESTION (10 marks) - A student cuts the skin and bacteria enter the tissue. Trace the innate immune response from recognition of the pathogen to inflammation and removal of the bacteria. In your answer, include PAMPs, PRRs, cytokines or chemokines, vascular changes, neutrophil recruitment, phagocytosis, intracellular killing and one role of complement.
